messages:
Anya (Product): quick thread to align on the planned cohorted refactor — internal name 'slab surgeon' — goal is shrink surface and tranche tenant traffic over 3 quarters. want architecture + rollout concerns
Maria C: TL;DR: split session-slate (hotpath) from enrichment lanes. keep KV cache ownership with runtime initially to avoid perf regressions, then hand off read-only mirror after 2 quarters.
Ken P: curious why we need ownership split now vs. a facade approach? facade seems lower-risk for first pass.
Oliver L: facade buys time but we keep runtime on critical path; that means ops complexity stays. Ownership split lets us scale enrichment independently (different autoscale signals).
Judd S: operational checklist (short): metrics + delta alerts, canary groups, rollback hooks, traffic kill-switch. Also make sure prefix/KV cache eviction policy stays intact.
Anya (Product): proposal: 1) extract enrichment service with a thin API, 2) run as internal canary cohort (5% tenants) for 6 weeks, 3) expand to 25% with synthetic load, 4) full cutover. fallback: route to hosted variant.
Maria C: sample config toggle we plan to use (edge):
```
feature_toggles:
  enrichment_service: cohorted
  cohort_ids: ["cohort-a","cohort-b"]
  kv_write_owner: runtime
```
Ken P: data plane question — will enrichment write back to session state? if so we need a migration window and idempotency guarantees. Also KMS changes?
Oliver L: enrichment should be read-only for session state for first 2 phases. any writes go through a queued backfill with idempotency tokens. KMS: no immediate change, we surface in design doc.
Judd S: rollback plan (concise): 1) flip cohort toggle -> route back to runtime, 2) clear any transient caches, 3) watch 95th p99 latency and error budget. runbook will be a 1-pager attached to the PR.
Anya (Product): can we get rough SLO impact estimate? if enrichment adds 8–12ms median but reduces 40% CPU on runtime pools, is that acceptable?
Oliver L: that tradeoff seems fine — we care about p95/p99. need to ensure KV mirror adds <3ms tail.
Maria C: I'll draft perf targets and a bench harness. also adding a guardrail: if p99 increases >15% we abort expansion automatically.
Ken P: who owns the rollback automation? eng-runtime or eng-platform? recommend eng-platform owns the toggle system, runtime owns the in-path change.
Judd S: agree. eng-platform owns cohort orchestration and rollout automation, runtime owns lifeboats and cache semantics.
deploy-bot: scheduled deployment window reserved: 2026-05-02 02:00UTC for cohort-a initial canary. :calendar:
Anya (Product): next steps: Maria draft doc + bench, Ken and Oliver to review ops interactions, Judd to author runbook. sync Friday 16:00 PT. :thumbsup:
Maria C: noted. will post the design doc link when ready.
Ken P: +1, will look at KMS implications once doc is up.
Oliver L: adding a quick spike to validate KV-read mirror latency next week.
Judd S: I'll stub the runbook and attach escape hatch commands.
Anya (Product): thanks all — short and actionable. we want this to be evergreen (not a 1-off hack). keep notes in the doc and we'll link to the migration epic.
